checks.note: max deviation 0.00%; the identity needs sum = 100%

checks.title: Same TMA metric version
checks.note: node definitions must match across cases

checks.title: EMON event multiplexing reliability
checks.note: below 95% the multiplexed TMA events are unreliable

checks.title: Same core frequency
checks.note: max deviation 0.03%; otherwise beta must include the frequency ratio

checks.title: Same CPU utilization (beta = 1)
checks.note: EMON-window utilization differs (beta_emon furthest from 1: 0.878) but steady-state beta was given; the EMON window likely includes idle time outside the workload

checks.title: EMON CPI consistent with the score model

values.4k-nothp vm: implied alpha +10.7%; user-mode CPI ratio 0.947 vs total 0.928
values.2m vm: CPI ratio 1.041 vs model 0.957 (+8.7%); user-mode CPI ratio 1.057 vs total 1.041
values.2m ept 2m text: implied alpha +10.7%; user-mode CPI ratio 1.070 vs total 1.053

checks.note: 4k-nothp vm: EMON CPI implies +10.7% instructions per unit of work vs the baseline; 2m vm: EMON CPI ratio deviates +8.7% from r(1+alpha)/beta; 2m ept 2m text: EMON CPI implies +10.7% instructions per unit of work vs the baseline; the same implied alpha in every compared case points at the baseline window rather than at the VMs (see the window check); a user-mode CPI ratio that deviates like the total one means the workload code itself runs at a different speed in that window (another phase). TMA ratios may include non-workload activity (misaligned window, idle polling, extra kernel/hypervisor code); alpha cancels out of the breakdown itself

checks.title: EMON windows cover comparable parts of the runs
checks.note: the baseline window covers about 28% of its run by busy time and 26% by user instructions, while the compared windows agree with whole runs (busy time tracks 1/r within 1%); this contradicts the same_phase answer. TMA of a partial window may not represent the scored run

checks.title: Same instruction mix (branches, loads, stores per instr)
checks.note: same binary and input expected; a uniform shift means non-workload instructions of another mix (about the size of the shift) or a different binary. With a CPI mismatch and an unchanged mix, suspect windows covering different phases rather than extra instructions

checks.title: Same uncore frequency
checks.note: shared resources outside the core model; differences limit the method

checks.title: Same DDR data rate
checks.note: shared resources outside the core model; differences limit the method

checks.title: Kernel share of busy time
checks.note: increase 3.26 points vs the baseline; kernel/hypervisor work is part of the VM cost

checks.title: Throughput workload: score is proportional to 1/elapsed time, same copies/threads and same score metric in every case
VM-case EMON was collected on the host, system-wide, without a guest/host mode filter (TMA covers guest, hypervisor and transition cycles)
EMON windows of all cases cover comparable parts of their runs (all whole runs, or all the same steady-state range)
checks.note: answered yes, but the window check refutes it

checks.title: All CPUs are busy in steady state: no single-thread critical section, I/O, sleep or off-CPU wait dominates
